title: The Poor Man's Cry and the Blessedness of Sharing
english: Pay attention. For I ask you to be pleased to rescue [me], not for the sake of another, but so that you might attend to helping me. And help me, if you make [me] outside of those ruling wars.

Those seeking my soul were greatly ashamed and were simultaneously ensnared. They were saying that the Psalm is about a single person. But if the one speaking is a man, he sends up a prayer concerning both, both for the body and for the soul. Therefore, if 'the Son of Man'—the Temple who has come forth from Mary—says these things, we shall say to those saying that only the body was taken: 'But He said, "He shall keep my body"'—see, even this He says, and it is the same person who is announcing it. Those who know the truth are turned back and are ashamed.

Those wishing evil upon me turned back toward the rear and were ensnared. It is a great thing to have turned the evil toward the rear; for to continue onward is harmful. Therefore, 'turning toward the rear' means 'they turned back' so as not to increase the road, not to rush forward. May those saying to me, 'Well done, well done,' be immediately clothed in shame. There is a wish regarding what he says, 'immediately,' that they may not remain in the evil, that they may not unceasingly say, 'Well done, well done, well done.' To say 'well done, well done' mockingly when something unpleasant is happening to those suffering is [wrong].

May all those seeking you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad. Having spoken concerning the adversaries, so that they also might be ashamed and be ensnared and turn toward the rear, saying mockingly 'well done, well done,' he says: 'May all those seeking you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad.' Then we rejoice and are glad when, having sought, we find you; for he who seeks something rejoices and is glad when he finds it. Even if, therefore, troublesome or other harmful things come upon [us], we seek to find you as a help. Then, appearing to be a help, you say: 'I will say while you are still speaking: Behold, I am here.'

And let them say at all times: Let the Lord be magnified. Since, having found you, they give thanks, saying, 'Let them say at all times: Let the Lord be magnified,' they might have those things for which they owe praise and rejoicing. It is possible to 'say at all times'; may ingratitude never exist for them. Those who love your salvation. The justice...
salvation, or the cause becoming salvation to them, or about to become salvation. 'Let the Lord be magnified always, let them say.' Loving your salvation, they magnify God always because of it.

18 But I am poor and needy; the Lord cares for me. Therefore I pray that your help may come to me and that you may be pleased to rescue me, because 'I am poor and needy.' I am not able to encourage myself, I am not able to do for myself from the outside regarding the things lying ahead, unless you help. 'Poor' therefore 'I am, and needy.' The difference between these two has been said at other times.

18 You are my helper and my protector; you are my God, do not delay. Since I have called you as a helper and a protector putting forth your shield for me—and this is the truth; for 'truth shall surround you as a weapon' (Ps 5:12)—'do not delay,' lest the struggle become too much for my strength. When you know it is the right time to care, to help, and to rescue, let this happen; for as far as my power and my nature reach, I am weak to help myself, to do for myself regarding the impending evils.

290 1–2 To the end; a psalm of David. Blessed is he who shows compassion to the poor and needy. And many take this psalm from the person of the Savior because of the way words lying here are received in the Gospel as having been spoken by the Savior and having been done and seen concerning the Savior. 'Blessed,' he says, 'is he who shows compassion to the poor and needy.' And many have explained such things regarding the character of the act, saying: the needy and the poor are different; and he who shares with these ought, according to analogy, to practice sharing; for he acts with understanding. It is not necessary to feed all those who are in want. Nor is it the case of one lacking food because he previously sought it thoughtlessly—he indulged in drinking, and everything he had he consumed unseemly and foolishly—but rather [one lacking] because of sickness or because of much childhood dependency. It is therefore necessary to provide to each with understanding. If anyone does not have enough to give to all, he ought to do this with understanding to those to whom he is obligated to give; and if he is able, he should also become a benefactor to others, according to the Father in the heavens, who causes the sun to rise not only upon the good but also upon the evil (Matt 5:45).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Body as a Bed of Suffering
english: However, since one cannot satisfy everyone, let him do this with understanding. This can be understood regarding the Savior: for he 'became poor through us' [2 Cor 8:9] and not for the sake of another. 'He became poor through us' so that he might free us from poverty and turn us away from want. He says, 'the one who did not know sin, for our sake made sin' [2 Cor 5:21]—this is his poverty—'so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.' [Fragmentary text] It was asked... it was not sustained. Even if sin occurred, it was not so that sin might remain, but so that he might free the... 'You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor for us' [2 Cor 8:9]. And the paradox is this: 'being rich' he is poor, and this poverty makes us rich, for it is a creative poverty. He is not poor at all, but in relation to his wealth.

2 In a day of evil the Lord will deliver him. He delivered Jesus 'in a day of evil' [Matt 27:22-23], when those surrounding him were saying, 'Crucify, crucify him; we have no king but Caesar.' And it was also asked from that evil day, how he, having become sin, became a creator of righteousness. The name of understanding is taken for the sake of doing good to brothers in need; for the apostle says regarding an offering: 'Understand what I say; for God will give you understanding in all things' [1 Cor 12:8]. And understanding is the knowledge of things joined together and things not joined together. Joined things are those that are similar, those that are equal, when we bring one thing to another and find that it has identity either by similarity or by equality. The one, therefore, having understanding, knows which things are joined to which and which are not.

3 The Lord will preserve him and let him live and make him blessed in the land. This can be said of both: the Lord preserves the poor and the needy. For this reason he also led the one understanding into himself. Where has it ever been said: when you see a suffering person and one who has arrived suddenly under another pretext, look there for a physician; see that the word of the divine providence has touched the physician, a compassionate physician, so that, sympathizing with the sufferer, he might help him medically. But he blesses the poor and needy man and makes him live in the land, or the one understanding and having received understanding upon...

The poor and the needy. If you speak concerning the Savior, you protect him and provide for him to live; for even though 'he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God' (Heb 13:3). Take 'in the earth' in a common sense.

And do not hand him over into the hands of his enemies. Such a person does not hand over 'into the hands of his enemies.' Such a person has many enemies, many who are attacking him; for he is a blessed man and has understanding toward the poor and the needy according to all the clarifications provided, and he has many [enemies] attacking him; for God will rescue him from their hands. But he who is given over to them is not rescued from the hand of those persecuting him.

The Lord will help him upon his bed of pain. Here, concerning the poor, he says: even if he should be upon a bed of sickness and such a thing should be painful to him, God helps him. Have the things said in the Gospels concerning the paralytics: one remained in a bed of pain for thirty-eight years, thrown down on a bed so as not to be able to be shaken or to rise up (John 5:5). And others like these were recorded in the Gospels as paralytics. But not everyone upon a bed of pain and sickness is rescued. For instance, one fell from the bed from on high and died.

But if toward a restoration, the body is often called the bed of the soul. And there are many scriptures gathered together for such a theory. When someone is in the corruptible body and dwells in the earth, he 'reaps a much-wise mind' (Job 4:7), [he] is 'upon a bed of pain'; but when God helps him, he makes him to lift up the body and to carry it away, and he is no longer thrown down upon the body, but he himself afterwards lifts up the bed and walks. The body, therefore, is a bed.

The lover of pleasure, the lover of passion, the one accepting and doing the things of the body, suffers upon a bed, but God helps him and makes him healthy, so that, having become healthy, he may no longer be thrown down upon the bed himself, but he himself may carry it, and as they say, so that the soul may begin of the body. What then are those sixty powerful ones, who are received in blessing, who are around the bed? From Abraham to nineteen and from... these, therefore, are the sixty powerful ones concerning the body of...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Sin against God and the Enemies of the Savior
english: Having served the Savior by his birth. It must be said thus: the world came into being in six days, and sixty is a perfect number, as it has been often demonstrated; for in tens, sixty-six is [present]. Therefore, he who surpassed the world and having gone above is able, being a 'man trained for war' (Ps 45:3), having a sword 'upon his thigh' (Ps 45:3). Concerning the bed of Solomon, these sixty are able, concerning the Lord's body, circling it, observing, by what cause the Savior was incarnated. 'Sixty' therefore [are] 'able around it, all holding a sword'. They are swords. And the swords which the wise hold are swords. 'The righteous shall rejoice in glory and shall exult in their throat' (Ps 97:11), 'and a two-edged sword in their hands' (Ps 45:3). They have two-edged swords in their hands. And they also have [it] 'upon the thigh'.

And since the drama concerning the marriage of the bride and bridegroom is a bridal chamber, he says the temperate ones concerning the bridegroom, to show, and he says that they have a sword upon the thigh, cutting away shameful desires. 'You turned his whole bed in his sickness' (Job 33:25). This says: he did not give a brief healing to the one greatly sickened, but 'turned his whole bed' (Job 33:25) away from the sickness, so that he might no longer be sick, but might be healthy, as I said concerning the paralytic. And you also say concerning Lazarus, the one being drawn out having a body, that, when he was taken up from thence by the angels, his whole bed was turned, his whole sickness. He was no longer laid down in sickness. Instead, he was being carried into the bosom of Abraham.

'I said, Lord, have mercy on me' (Ps 51:3). Instead, he says that: what was upon us was achieved, to be rescued from the bed of sickness and to be helped from the bed of pain; for I did this, 'I said, Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you' (Ps 51:3). You see that, when he sinned, then he was in [trouble] and then he was laid upon a bed and a couch. When therefore anyone knows Him who is able to rescue, he will attain to the one who is striving, similarly to him: 'I want, be cleansed' (Mark 1:41), 'Rise, take up your bed and walk' (Mark 2:11). 'I' therefore 'said, Lord, have mercy' (Ps 51:3). By saying: 'Lord, have mercy on me', I showed that I was not able to be pitied by myself. I healed.

I have sinned against you, I have sinned against you. In this way, almost all of us sin toward God, knowing much about Him through ignorance and doing much contrary to His laws. 'I have sinned' is thus 'against you'; but having said, 'Lord, have mercy on me,' he possesses the petition.

My enemies said evil things to me: 'When will he die, and will his name be destroyed?' (Ps 54:1). I say that this psalm is to be spoken from the person of the Savior according to man. And since the Jews have become His enemies, like traitors to the truth, having not understood the one who came among them, and since Judas also became one of the disciples, regarding the enemies he speaks singularly of those having risen up against him—once in reference to Judas as the beginning of the betrayal, and once plurally because of those following him and having overthrown Jesus.

And it is not only here that this happens, but also in the 108th psalm it is said: 'They spoke against me with a deceitful tongue, and with words of hatred they surrounded me. Instead of loving me, they attacked me, but I was praying; and they set evil against me instead of good, and hatred instead of my love. Set the sinner upon him, and let the devil stand at his right hand' (Ps 108:2-5)—this he says singularly concerning Judas—'in the judging of him, let him go out condemned, and let another take his oversight' (Ps 108:8). Once therefore concerning Judas, and once concerning those who agreed with him, he speaks; and for this reason in the same verses where there is singular, there is plural.

And thus he says: 'My enemies said.' This they said: the evil things which they think are evil, they said against me: 'When will he die, and will his name be destroyed?' (Ps 54:1). For they thought that after the death of Jesus his teaching and his fame would be extinguished, and they said: 'When will he die?' On the contrary, it went the opposite of what they thought. His name did not shine forth less when he lived and was alive than when he was crucified and taken up. And for the correction of those of heterodox opinion, this is to be taken: for as many as do not think rightly, but are being deceived and say impious things concerning the Savior, they are the ones who spoke evil against him. And since there is a leader of the heresies, the false speaker, or even his slandering devil, through...
